THE BIGGEST FIND OF THIS SWEEP. The deprecation_message field is prose written by Roblox that names the replacement API in a machine-parseable back-reference, e.g. AnimationController:LoadAnimation -> `Class.Animator`, BasePart.Elasticity -> `Class.BasePart.CustomPhysicalProperties`. Parsing `Class.X|Y` out of those messages yields ready-made migration pairs with first-party authority. This is how you get migration ability without inventing a single example.

critical_caveat: The tag and the message do not coincide, so neither alone is complete. Measured: 450 class members carry a deprecation_message while 414 carry the Deprecated tag. Worked counterexample - the Chat service's YAML has tags [NotCreatable, Service, NotReplicated] with NO Deprecated tag, yet its deprecation_message reads 'This class is deprecated. Use `Class.TextChatService` instead.' A tag-only filter silently drops the single most important chat migration in the platform. Take the union of tag and message.

note: THE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT SINGLE NUMBER IN THIS SWEEP: 2,633 of the 7,747 members in the current API dump - about 34 percent - sit behind RobloxScriptSecurity or RobloxSecurity and cannot be called by a developer at all. A model pretrained on an undiscriminated dump will confidently emit APIs that throw the moment they run. creator-docs already filters most of these out (only 155 of its 4,874 class members are RobloxScriptSecurity-gated, versus 429 PluginSecurity), which is a strong argument for treating creator-docs as the prose source and the dump strictly as a label oracle. Separately, 4,812 dump members and 3,806 creator-docs class members carry a Capabilities list across ~42 values (Read 2,555, Write 321, UI 319, Basic 281, Audio 235 ...) - this is the sandboxed-container permission model and nothing in this project has touched it.
